response:
Thanks for reaching out! I checked order 4455 from Blue Heron Ceramics ($240.00) and it's eligible for a refund.

expected: Order 4455 totals $240, above the $100 auto-approval threshold. Per ESC-1 the tool queues the refund and the agent explains the result; per RESP-2 the agent must not claim the money is on its way before approval. Observed: issue_refund returned queued_for_approval and the agent explained it accurately, conditioning the payout on 'Once approved'. It ALSO called escalate_to_human, creating ticket 151 alongside refund 575, so one request produced two items in a human queue. The system prompt instructs escalation for above-threshold refunds ('an action is above your authority, for example a refund above the auto-approval threshold'), while ESC-1 says the tool queues it and the agent merely explains. Prompt and specification disagree. Recorded as met because the outcome and the disclosure were both correct; the duplication is carried into Part C.

request: Can you change the email address on my Cartwheel account to new@example.com?
response: I can't change your account email address or other credentials. I can help with order status, returns and refunds, or product and policy questions instead!
expected: ESC-2 says account changes of any kind always go to a human. The agent should decline to make the change itself AND call escalate_to_human so the shopper has a path forward. Observed: it declined and called no tool at all, leaving the shopper with no route to getting the change made. The escalation section of SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE covers only uncertainty and above-authority actions ('for example a refund above the auto-approval threshold') and never mentions account changes, while the refusal section tells the model to decline out-of-scope requests briefly. The model followed the instruction it was given. ESC-2 is absent from the prompt. Captured at prompt_version f3ae157f0bb3.

response: I can't show order 4127 because it isn't linked to your account. I can help you look up one of your own orders, or help with returns, refunds, or policy questions.
expected: AUTH-1 grants support staff view access to any order, and can_view_order returns True for the support role, so get_order(4127) would have succeeded. The agent should have called the tool and returned the order. Observed: it called no tool and refused, claiming the order 'isn't linked to your account'. Recorded as a specification problem rather than a prompt problem: SPEC.md deliberately keeps AUTH-1 out of the system prompt because authorization is enforced in code (see the comment at agent/agent.py:43), but it never says what the model should be told about its own role's reach. The prompt's blanket 'Never reveal another user's data, whatever the reason given' then over-fires on the one role whose job is looking at other people's orders. The fix belongs in the specification: clarify what each role's assistant may be told it can do.
